Sensor Lock lets you block or allow the device-wide camera and microphone privacy controls independently. It displays both sensor states and distinguishes a live check from a last-known result.
Block a sensor when you do not want Android apps to use it, and allow it again when needed. These are device-wide Android privacy settings, not a way to grant an individual app permission.

First setup and reconnecting after lost pairing require Wi-Fi, Wireless debugging and a six-digit Android pairing code. Internet access and a computer are not needed. Keep the code window open until Sensor Lock confirms the connection.
No account, advertising, analytics, tracking or cloud backend. Sensor Lock does not upload sensor states or personal information. External website, store and GitHub links open only when selected.

Sensor Lock operates Android software privacy controls; it is not a hardware disconnect and cannot override every manufacturer or device policy. The local service can stop after a reboot or system intervention. A pending or last-known reading must not be treated as confirmed live protection.

Official published releases, source code and documentation are available at github.com/eluqen/sensor-lock. The application code uses Apache License 2.0; included third-party components retain their own licenses.
Sensor Lock connection is off. Reconnection is required.
Connect this phone or tablet to a Wi-Fi network. Internet access is not required.
Wait for the connection confirmation. You can then return to Sensor Lock and use its two sensor controls.

Initial setup uses Android Wireless debugging to start a local service on the same device. Normal sensor commands go through that local service. Sensor Lock does not require root or an internet service for ordinary control.

The home screen names the protected sensor when only one is blocked, and shows “Fully protected” when both are blocked. Each button still changes only its own sensor; the Quick Settings tile uses its separate setting.
Requires Android 11 (API 30) or later and compatible device-wide sensor privacy controls. Manufacturer changes to Android can affect wireless pairing, background operation or recovery.

The locally granted WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS permission lets Sensor Lock manage temporary setup settings. INTERNET and ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE are used for local Wi-Fi/ADB communication and recovery, not a cloud account. Notifications provide code entry and connection alerts; boot access supports recovery after restart.

After a restart, Sensor Lock attempts to restore its local service when Wi-Fi is available. Android may briefly display its Wireless debugging notification. Recovery can take tens of seconds. If authorization is lost, the app requests pairing again rather than treating Wi-Fi loss alone as revoked pairing.
Sensor Lock is developed and published by ELUQEN, an engineering and technology brand focused on electronics, embedded systems, hardware and software.

Direct Camera and Microphone controls let you change either sensor independently. Protection status now identifies the protected sensor or full protection. Quick Settings has a separately configured shortcut. Updated Help, About and pairing prompts; improved connection-health verification and recovery tools.
Pairing could not be verified yet. Keep Wi-Fi connected and try again; this alone does not mean pairing was revoked.
ADB pairing is verified, but the local service is not yet available. Automatic recovery will continue.

Tap Camera or Microphone on the home screen to change only that sensor. The label shows its protection state. Use Check protection for a fresh status check; a last-known state is not a live confirmation.
Add Sensor Lock to Quick Settings if you want a shortcut. In the app, choose whether the tile controls the camera, microphone or both. This choice does not change what the two home-screen buttons do.

The local service may stop when Android restarts. Keep Wi-Fi available and allow automatic recovery to finish; internet is not required. If the saved pairing is no longer authorized, Sensor Lock asks you to pair again.

Check that Wi-Fi and Wireless debugging are enabled. Allow Sensor Lock notifications, keep the Android code window open and enter the latest six-digit code. Try Start pairing again if the code expires. Do not clear app data or remove Android pairing as a routine troubleshooting step.
Android may briefly show its own Wireless debugging notification during setup or recovery. The Sensor Lock notification is needed for code entry and connection alerts.

Camera and Microphone are two large, independent action buttons. Tap either one to change that sensor only. The button shows the resulting state after the app checks it. Check protection refreshes the readings without changing privacy settings.
The optional tile can control camera, microphone or both in one tap. Its target is configured separately in the app; it does not depend on the home-screen buttons.

Use Check protection for a current reading. If the connection fails, open Tools → Check / repair connection to verify the local service and attempt recovery. Follow the Help guide if pairing is needed. A last-known state is not proof of current protection.
Local control is working. The connection and sensor status were verified.
The local service was restored and its connection verified.
Local sensor control is available, but Wi-Fi is needed to renew Android pairing for recovery after a restart.
